The journey to the summit begins at Praia Vermelha. The first cable car climbs to Urca, and the second continues to Sugarloaf Mountain. Even during the ascent, you can see the city curving around green slopes and reaching the water.

From the top, the views take in Botafogo Bay, the Copacabana coastline and the entrance to Guanabara Bay. The cable car has operated since 1912 and has become one of Rio's symbols. The summit itself is easy to recognize by its rounded shape and steep granite slopes.

A visit to Sugarloaf Mountain can be part of a city sightseeing tour or a separate trip to the viewpoints. The timing of the ascent, tickets and stops depend on the particular itinerary.

Sucre is one of Bolivia's most beautiful cities and its official capital, although the government buildings are located in the country's other capital, La Paz. The abundance of white colonial buildings has earned Sucre the nickname "White City."

The city stands in a high-altitude area of a white limestone plateau. Its rich architecture, quiet picturesque streets and relaxed atmosphere make a striking impression. Sucre's principal attractions are closely connected with its colonial past. The Spanish left behind grand mansions and palaces, many of which now house museums and hotels.

Plaza 25 de Mayo is the city's most visited square. It is home to the cathedral and city hall, as well as a monument to Antonio José de Sucre, the second president of independent Bolivia. Numerous shops and souvenir stalls offer interesting finds, while restaurants serve local cuisine: indigenous dishes with a Spanish touch. Meat is a regular feature of the menu, including pork, beef and alpaca, alongside potatoes and corn. A favorite local drink is chicha, a beer made from corn.

Sumidero lies in Chiapas and is known for the high walls that flank its river. A boat ride reveals the canyon from below: water stretches ahead while rock slopes rise on both sides. This perspective allows visitors to appreciate the gorge's shapes and vegetation.

The canyon adds a natural stop to a journey between Tuxtla Gutiérrez and San Cristóbal. The river, rock and height of the banks are the main attractions here. Sumidero offers a different side of Chiapas from city streets and archaeological complexes, while highlighting the region's mountainous landscape.

## Ciudad del Este: a duty-free shopping hub!

Originally named after a former dictator, the city has struggled to shed its reputation as one of South America's most corrupt cities. It forms part of the so-called Tri-Border Area, a duty-free trading zone.

## Ciudad del Este: a destination for shoppers!

The city's principal attractions are its shops, with inexpensive electronics, cigarettes and alcoholic drinks, as well as excellent snack bars. Much of the population is of Asian origin, including Thai and Korean residents, as well as Arabs and Iranians; the city therefore has many mosques and pagodas. The construction of the Itaipu hydroelectric power plant, described as the world's most powerful, contributed to the city's rapid growth. The Friendship Bridge across the Paraná River links Ciudad del Este with the neighboring Brazilian city of Foz do Iguaçu. Opened in 1965, it measures a little over 552 meters and also serves as a border crossing, enclosed along its perimeter by a tall fence.
